newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Oil prices rise, defying bearish stocks data.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Oil prices rise, defying bearish stocks data.

text.p: World oil prices advanced on Wednesday in a gravity-defying technical rally that brushed aside bearish news of growing U.S. crude oil inventories.
April futures for benchmark North Sea Brent Blent crude oil in London traded at $19.56 a barrel at 1630 GMT, up 32 cents on the day.
Prices briefly dipped below the psychological $19 level in reaction to data showing a rise in crude stocks in the United States, but U.S. crude futures drove the market higher half an hour later.

"It's partly the psychology of the market," said Charles Gray at Prudential Bache Futures in London. "Typically on Wednesdays New York follows in the direction of the stock numbers for the first 20 minutes or so after they come out, and then they run out of steam."
"Fundamentally everyone is flat-footed here because they expected everything to go lower," he added. "But sometimes the tecnhicals lead the fundamentals and this is the case here."
The dominance of technical factors was made possible by the absence of other oil-related news that could have moved the market either way.
A report by the American Petroleum Institute showed crude oil stocks rose to 304.62 million barrels in the week to March 7, up from 297.78 million barrels the previous week.
A separate report from the U.S. Energy Information Administration said crude stocks rose 5.2 million barrels to 305.1 million barrels in the same period.

Traders added the market preferred to focus on slightly bullish oil product data showing a drop in U.S. gasoline output as the industry gears up for the spring and summer driving seasons. Production fell 137,000 barrels per day in the latest week to 7.24 million bpd.

A growing glut of crude production aggravated by a mild winter weather has knocked 19 percent off Brent's value since January 1, ending a six-month rally that took prices to their highest levels in six years.
But the bellwether crude now appears to be consolidating near $19.50 after failing to fall decisively below $19 in the past 10 days.
Key Atlantic Basin spot markets are weighted down by a glut of unsold North Sea and west African crude cargoes. Spot price differentials for a range of crude grades are shrinking.

Geoff Pyne of UBS Global Research wrote in a monthly report that world supply of crude oil in February exceeded that of a year ago by 2.7 million barrels per day, while world demand grew only 1.8 million bpd in the same period.

"Recent output is already greater than most late-1996 forecasts of the likely 1997 average," he said, adding that after nine months of crude shortage, crude stocks are gradually returning to comfortable levels.
"It is hard to find factors for bulls to pin hopes to," he said.
